bib.title: REACT: SYNERGIZING REASONING AND ACTING IN LANGUAGE MODELS

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Fever/ALFWorld/WebShop example trajectories (App D) and error examples (App E) skimmed not read line by line.

question: Can an LLM that interleaves free-form reasoning traces with task actions solve knowledge-intensive and interactive decision tasks better than reasoning-only or acting-only prompting?
hypothesis: Reasoning traces help the model induce, track and update action plans and handle exceptions, while actions let it ground reasoning in external information, so the two together beat either alone.
contributions: ReAct, a prompt-based paradigm to synergize reasoning and acting in language models for general task solving
Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks showing advantage in few-shot setup over reasoning-only or action-only approaches
Systematic ablations on the importance of acting in reasoning tasks and reasoning in interactive tasks
Analysis of limitations under prompting and initial finetuning experiments

method.summary: A frozen PaLM-540B is prompted with 1-6 hand-written few-shot trajectories of thought/action/observation to solve HotpotQA and Fever through a three-action Wikipedia API, and ALFWorld and WebShop with sparse thoughts. Baselines are ablations of the same trajectories (Standard, CoT, CoT-SC, Act), plus ReAct+CoT-SC hybrids and a small bootstrapped finetuning study on PaLM-8B/62B.
method.task: Multi-hop QA, fact verification, text game, web shopping navigation

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.size: 6 training cases used as exemplars; full eval size not stated (Table 5 uses a 500-question validation subset)

datasets.name: FEVER
datasets.size: 3 training cases as exemplars; eval size not stated

datasets.name: ALFWorld
datasets.size: 134 unseen evaluation games; 3 annotated trajectories per task type (6 task types)
datasets.preprocessing: 6 prompts per task type from each ordered permutation of 2 of the 3 trajectories

datasets.name: WebShop
datasets.size: 500 test instructions; 1.18M products, 12k human instructions in the environment

datasets.name: HotpotQA finetuning set
datasets.size: 3,000 trajectories with correct answers generated by ReAct (also for the other methods)
datasets.source: self-generated by PaLM-540B prompting, bootstrapping as in STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022)

other.train: 10^5 expert trajectories per task type, beam search, results from their Table 4
IL: 1,012 human trajectories; IL+RL additionally 10,587 training instructions

training.objective: inferred: supervised finetuning on whole trajectories (thoughts, actions, observations) conditioned on question/claim
training.steps: PaLM-8B: ReAct and Act 4,000 steps, Standard and CoT 2,000; PaLM-62B: ReAct and Act 4,000, Standard and CoT 1,000

other.scope: finetuning only for HotpotQA; main results are prompting only (no training)

inference.decoding: greedy for ReAct/Act/CoT (Table 3 caption: all methods use greedy decoding except BUTLER beam search; Table 5 greedy)
inference.samples: CoT-SC: 21 CoT samples majority vote; ALFWorld: 6 prompt permutations per task type, avg and best of 6 reported; seeds not stated
inference.prompting: Few-shot: 6 (HotpotQA), 3 (Fever), 2 of 3 annotated per ALFWorld task type (6 perms), 1-shot WebShop. Thoughts dense on QA, sparse on ALFWorld/WebShop (model decides).
inference.retrieval: Wikipedia API: search[entity] returns first 5 sentences of page or top-5 similar entities; lookup[string] returns next sentence containing string; finish[answer]

parameters.react_to_cot_sc_step_limit: 7 steps HotpotQA, 5 steps FEVER (ReAct->CoT-SC fallback when no answer in those steps)
parameters.cot_sc_to_react_trigger: majority answer among n CoT-SC samples occurs fewer than n/2 times
parameters.cot_sc_n: 21 in Table 1; Fig 2 sweeps up to 20 trials

other.footnote: Of correct trajectories, those with 7 steps on HotpotQA and 5 steps on FEVER are 0.84% and 1.33%

metrics.name: WebShop score
metrics.definition: average percentage of desired attributes covered by chosen product

metrics.name: WebShop success rate (SR)
metrics.definition: percentage of episodes where chosen product satisfies all requirements

eval.protocol: Single run per prompt on QA tasks, no significance tests or seeds reported; ALFWorld 6 prompts, avg and best of 6 (BUTLER best of 8); Table 2 manual study of 200 trajectories.

availability.code: https://react-lm.github.io/ (project page with code); anonymous repo for GPT-3 ReAct code in reproducibility statement

Full 6 exemplars in App C.1

prompts.purpose: ALFWorld ReAct exemplar: thoughts as '> think:' lines interleaved with actions such as '> go to fridge 1'; Act prompt same without think lines; ReAct-IM has repeated dense subgoal restatements. Full exemplars Tables 7-9

limits: Main experiments use PaLM-540B, not openly available; GPT-3 check only on HotpotQA subset and ALFWorld.
Prompted ReAct is worst of four methods at PaLM-8B/62B; needs strong models or finetuning.
ReAct is more error-prone in reasoning than CoT (47% vs 16%, including repetitive loops) and a bad search result derails it (23% of errors).
Authors suspect loops come from greedy decoding.
Complex tasks with large action spaces need more demonstrations than in-context length allows.
Prompting methods remain far from supervised SoTA (67.5 EM HotpotQA) and expert humans on WebShop.
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; HotpotQA labels can be outdated.
Wikipedia API deliberately weak (exact page names), not a strong retriever.
